name: Rudel
prior: No playable wolf-howl instrument found in two passes (standard + extended). Nearest: Boscomac 'The Howler' (Reaktor, screaming feedback/distortion synth, not a howl; VS: rekkerd.org/boscomac-releases-the-howler-for-reaktor); 'Howl: A formant synthesizer' (iOS, human-voice formants, pitch-space keyboard; VS: apps.apple.com/app/id1067562312); Krotos Dehumaniser 2 (creature-voice PROCESSOR of a mic/recorded input: pitch shift, granular, 'Scrubbing Convolution' with a library of animal recordings - no synthesis; VS: krotosaudio.com dehumaniser-2-update, designingsound.org/2014/12/16/review-dehumaniser); 'Werewolf Howl & Sounds' (iOS sample player; VS: apps.apple.com/app/id345366423); Akai Rhythm Wolf ('Let it Howl' is a distortion; VS: akaipro.com/rhythm-wolf). Howl acoustics for calibration: Indian wolf howl mean F0 422 +/- 126 Hz, howls are long, with pitch variation over the call; chorus howls contain barks/squeaks/growls (VS: journals.plos.org pone.0216186; ncbi PMC4856277; britannica.com/science/howling). Verdict on prior art: the SOUND is ordinary sound-design territory (sine/saw + slow glide + vibrato + formant filter is the recipe the search results themselves recommend; trailer libraries are sample-based), the INSTRUMENT (tuned, held, self-assembling asynchronous pack with register breaks, playable polyphonically) was not found anywhere. In Myzel: Stimme (synchronous 3/6-singer glottal choir through 3 vowel formants, APP 4116-4200) is the direct sibling.
costNotes: Pure native node graph, same class as Stimme (stm = 1.05 measured, APP 2081: 3 PeriodicWave oscs + 3 bandpass + ~8 gains + noise + LFO). Rudel L1: 3 osc (cached PeriodicWave 'howl', A.waves) + 3 entry gains + 2 shared formant BQ + 1 pan + breath noise + BQ + gain = ~12 nodes at ~0.03-0.06 units each (R: webaudio.md section 4: 0.03 per native node, 1.0 for Nebel's 16) -> 0.7-1.0; the event planning (breaks, contours) is main-thread scheduling, free. L3 (6 howlers, 3 formants x 2 sides, 2 breaths) ~ 2.0, Stimme-L3 class (2.4). The idea's 1.0 / 1.9 is right. A worklet buys nothing here.
soundHeld: Done right this is a real gesture no instrument offers: hold the note and listen to the pack assemble, break, re-find the tone; two fingers = two packs; Bebung = natural howl vibrato on the detune bus. Done as specified it will sound like a cartoon dog: a 1/n-harmonic PeriodicWave with +4 dB on the 3rd/5th through two Q-5 formants is a sawtooth with a wah, whereas real howls are near-sinusoidal (strong F0 around 300-500 Hz, weak upper harmonics, breathy noise floor) with occasional subharmonic/biphonic breaks. The source must be 2-4 soft harmonics plus breath; the formants must stay above 1.3 f (the idea notes this). The assembling pack is slow by design: at y low the third howler enters after up to i*0.8*1.9*rand ~ 3-4 s, so the first two seconds of every held note are a single howl - fine for ambient, dead for chords. Hoehe changing the interval set (0/+700/+1200 ct) means finger height alters HARMONY, not timbre, which breaks Myzel's Hoehe convention (every other engine: Hoehe = timbre); a three-note keyboard chord with y high becomes 9 glides in fifths and octaves = mud. Contours via setValueCurveAtTime cannot be re-planned on setF without cancelScheduledValues and (on Firefox, no cancelAndHoldAtTime) a jump; use setTargetAtTime chains for contours. Breaks via exponentialRamp on detune are impossible when the ramp crosses or starts at 0 ct (spec: exponential ramps need same-sign nonzero values) - linearRamp or ramp the frequency param instead. The 1.2 s release must include a falling glide (howls fall off), or every note end sounds cut.
soundBurst: Puls = one howler with the contour squeezed to gate*0.6 and no breaks ('Klaeffen'): a tuned chirp f*2^(-5/12) -> f in ~60 ms through the formant pair. It is a plausible yelp and tempo-robust, but tuned yelps on a euclidean grid are a video-game dog within seconds; without the breath transient and a random per-hit contour depth it is just a pitch-enveloped saw. Short gates give no pack at all, so the engine's identity is absent from the Puls - acceptable if the lane is meant as a bark lane, but then the preset text must say so.
failureModes: Cartoon: 1/n-harmonic source + 3rd/5th boost through Q-5 formants = saw-with-wah; real howls are near-sine with breath. Source needs 2-4 soft harmonics, never exact unison, slow contours
Hoehe = interval set (0/+700/+1200 ct) changes harmony instead of timbre; keyboard chords with high y turn into 9 glides of fifths and octaves
First 2-4 s of a held note at low y is a single howl (asynchronous entry delays up to i*Ansatz*1.9*rand); the pack never forms for notes shorter than ~3 s
setValueCurveAtTime contours cannot be re-planned on setF; Firefox lacks cancelAndHoldAtTime -> jumps. Use setTargetAtTime chains
exponentialRampToValueAtTime on detune from/through 0 ct is invalid (same-sign nonzero required); breaks need linear ramps or the frequency param
Release without a falling glide sounds cut; howls end with a drop
Formants thin above ~1 kHz (idea notes 1.3 f minimum); the useful range is 150-800 Hz, so the preset must force v.oct -1 and the engine should fold high notes down
Puls identity: a lone tuned chirp per hit is generic; the engine's novelty (the pack) is inaudible in the sequencer
verdict: Rare: the howl SOUND is a ten-minute patch in any synth (glide + vibrato + formant) and a sample in every trailer library, but a tuned, held, self-assembling asynchronous pack with register breaks exists nowhere playable (Dehumaniser processes a voice, Howl is a human formant synth, The Howler is a feedback screamer). Native and cheap at about 0.95 units (Stimme class; 2.0 at level 3), no worklet needed. The held note can be a genuine new gesture if the source is near-sinusoidal with breath and the formants stay above 1.3 f; as specified (1/n harmonics, +4 dB on 3/5, Q-5 formants) it is a cartoon dog, and Hoehe choosing intervals makes finger height change harmony instead of timbre. The Puls hit is a plausible but generic tuned yelp that carries none of the pack idea; contours need setTargetAtTime chains (not setValueCurveAtTime) and linear (not exponential) detune ramps.
